what: Interaction: when the pointer enters a wide panel like the Contact box, the round button (180px) inside grows from half size over .5s ease-out and appears. Each frame it follows the cursor by 20% of the remaining distance, and a transform transition of .8s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1) slows it once more so it glides into place. When the pointer leaves, it shrinks back to half size and stays at its last position.

options.--fx-dur: Follow transition length (via style), default .8s — at 0s only lerp
options.--fx-ease: Follow-along transition curve (via style), default cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1)
options.--fx-from: Size ratio while hidden (via style), default .5
options.look: fade: Outside the board the button is transparent and hidden, and on entering it grows and appears over the same duration (brand)
options.--fx-pop-ease: Grow-and-appear curve (via style), default ease-out — Brand cubic-bezier(.25,.46,.45,1)
options.[data-fx-part=ring]: (if present) a ring that turns while it fills the button — one linear turn per --fx-spin (default 10s)

note: On touch devices (hover false) the button is hidden (the original also hides it when _isTouchDevice). With reduced motion on, it sits at the cursor right away with no delay

from.where: shared.js·shared.css .ft-contact__hit .ft-stalker (contact box on every page) — original main.js _cursor(): on every requestAnimationFrame e += .2*(mouseX - panel left - e), [data-js=stalker] transition .8s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1), inner circle scale .5→1 .5s ease-out

index.html two strategy guide cards .guide-card (data-fx=lerp-stalker) — original top.js mouseStoker(): on every gsap.ticker, pos += (mouse − pos) × (1 − (1 − .5)^deltaRatio), .stalker_link_box 164px transition transform 1.05s cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1). On card hover, is-active fades in the ring graphic (one turn per 10s) and the arrow with opacity 0→1 · scale .5→1 .35s cubic-bezier(.25,.46,.45,1).
from.note: In the original one circle floats over the whole window and shows only over cards. Here each card gets its own button to give the same look. The follow share is .5 per frame without frame-time correction (same at 60fps)
